<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />''found him'' {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מַ֫יִם רַבִּים|translate=by the great waters}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=16|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=20}}, and a still more remarkable instance in 8:30 {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מְקוֹם שִׁבְתְּךָ אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֫יִם}}. This combination of ''two'' different ideas, of motion ''to'' a place and being or acting ''in'' the place (very plainly seen in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=16|verse=6}} ''but to the place which the Lord thy God shall choose''... shalt thou bring thine offering and ''there shalt thou sacrifice'', &c.), is the same as the Greek use of εἰς, ἐς for ἐν, the Latin ''in potestatem, in amicitiam ditionemque esse, manere'' (Cic. Verr. 5, 38; Div. 2, 14, &c.); cf. also the common German expressions ''zu'' Hause, ''zu'' Leipzig sein, ''zu'' Bette liegen, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|h}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}.<ref>Cf. Wandel, ''De particulae Hebr.'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=indole, vi, usu}}, Jena, 1875.</ref> Underlying the very various uses of this preposition is either the idea of being or moving within some definite region, or some sphere of space or time (with the infinitive, a simultaneous action, &c.), or else the idea of ''fastening on'' something, ''close connexion with'' something (also in a metaphorical sense, following some kind of pattern, e.g. the advice or command of some one {{GHGheb|text=בִּדְבַר פ׳}}, {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽעֲצַת פ׳}}, or in a comparison, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּצַלְמֵ֫נוּ כִדְמוּתֵ֫נוּ|translate=in our image, after our likeness}}; cf. 1:27, 5:1, 3), or finally the idea of ''relying'' or ''depending'' upon..., or even of merely ''striking'' or ''touching'' something.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|i}}
Thus the use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} is explained—

(1) In the sense of ''among'' (in the domain of), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=יָשָׁר בָּֽאָדָם אָ֫יִן|translate=there is none upright among men}}; in the sense of ''consisting of'', in specifying the constituents of a collective idea, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=21}} ''and all flesh died''... ''in'' (=consisting of) ''fowl'', &c. 8:17, 9:10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=3}}. Also after ideas of ''appearing, manifesting oneself, representing, being'', in the sense of ''as, in the capacity of'' (prop. in the sphere, after the manner of, see above), ''consisting of''..., ''tanquam'', the {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=essentiae}} of the earlier grammarians, corresponding to the Greek ἐν, the Latin ''in'',<ref>e.g. ''res in praeda captae'', i.e. things taken as spoil; see Nägelsbach, ''Lat. Stilistik'', § 123:4. On the Hebrew {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=essentiae}}, see Hauschild in the ''Festschrift zur Einweihung des Goethegymn''. Frankf. a. M. 1897, p. 163.</ref> and the French ''en'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=3}} ''I appeared unto Abraham''... {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵל שַׁדָּי|translate=as El Shaddai}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהוּא בְאֶחָד|translate=but he is}} (manifests himself as) ''one'', i.e. he remains always the same; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=62|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּמְתֵי מְעָט|translate=in the condition of being few}}, cf. 10:22 ''to the number of seventy''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=7}}.—Cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=4}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=146|verse=5|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֶזְרִי|translate=as my help}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=14}} ''being unclean''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=16}} ''in Sion'' (i.e. ''I make Sion a foundation''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=41}} ''as a sweet savour''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=26}}, perhaps also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=2}} ''in'' (i.e. ''as'') ''a flame of fire''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=66|verse=15}} ''with'' (i.e. ''like'') ''fire''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=31|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=20|hidebook=1}} (102:4). For the origin of all these forms of expression {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=54|verse=6}} is especially instructive, since {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי בְּסֹֽמְכֵי נַפְשִׁי}} is not meant to refer to the Lord as ''belonging to'' the {{GHGheb|text=סֹֽמְכִים}}, but only to ascribe to him a similar character, i.e. ''the Lord is one who upholds my soul''; so also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=99|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=35}} [the plur. as in {{GHGpar|124|g}}–i].<ref>Other instances formerly cited here ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=19}}, where {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} is used before the subject) as well as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיָהּ שְׁמוֹ|translate=Jah is his name}}, are textually very uncertain. Cf. Cheyne, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}} Isaiah, p. 173, on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=4}}.</ref>—Cf. Gesenius, {{GHGcite|title=Thes. Linguae Hebr.}}, i. 174 f., and Delitzsch on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|k}}
(2) To introduce the object after transitive verbs, which denote ''touching, striking, reaching to'' (thus to some extent a fastening on, see above) something, in English sometimes rendered by ''at, on'', &c., and in German generally by compounds with ''an'', e.g. ''anfassen''={{GHGheb|text=אָחַז בְּ}}, ''anrühren''={{GHGheb|text=נָגַע בְּ}}, &c. To the same category belongs also the construction of verbs denoting ''authority'' ({{GHGheb|text=מָלַךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָשַׁל}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָגַשׂ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָדָה}}, the last prop. ''to tread on''...) with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, inasmuch as the exercise of the authority is regarded as a laying hold of the person ruled; so also, the introduction of the object by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} after certain {{GHGterm|verba dicendi}}, or when the mental action is to be represented as extending ''to'' some one or something: e.g.<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
